ud5.7:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud5.7:1.3: Then at that time venerable Kaṅkhārevata (Doubting Revata) was sitting not far away from the Fortunate One, after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, reflecting on his own purification through crossing over doubt. The Fortunate One saw venerable Kaṅkhārevata sat not far away, after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight,
ud5.7:2.1: reflecting on his own purification through crossing over doubt.
ud5.7:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud5.7:4.1: “Whatever doubts there are (about) here or hereafter,
ud5.7:4.2: Understandable by oneself, or understandable by another,
ud5.7:4.3: The meditators give up all these,
ud5.7:4.4: The ardent ones living the spiritual life.”
